title: Rapid resume: token throughput rescuer for cross-deployment TTFT drop
creator: Asha Patel
description: Production regression: starting 2026-03-09 07:10 UTC we observed a sustained drop in tokens/sec and TTFT increases across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments for several medium and long-form models. The pattern indicates increased priming / first-token latency on short prompt fanout and a correlated drop in steady-state token throughput for multi-variant fanout requests. Multiple customers (enterprise and mid-market) have opened escalations citing poor UX and SLA misses. This ticket drives triage, temporary rescue, and coordinated rollout of a guarded remediation across all deployment modes.
comments: 2026-03-10 07:45 UTC — Triage call: Platform SRE, Runtime, Routing, and SEs. Top hypotheses: (1) kernel selection heuristic change favored sparse-attn kernel on mixed-context batches, (2) KV-prefetch backpressure interacting with microbatch coalescer, (3) new warmup hedging rollout produced noisy warmstarts. Decided immediate action: enable narrow hedging guard, throttle prefetch for visible tenants, and add extra instrumentation for token latency distribution.

2026-03-10 09:20 UTC — Reproduced locally against model v3-medium and v4-long with archived traffic shape. Confirmed 20-40% drop in tokens/sec for weighted-multiplex bursts and median TTFT up ~180ms vs baseline. Added debug traces to kernel selector showing mis-score for quantized int8 paths on sequence length 64-256.

2026-03-10 11:05 UTC — Hotpatch plan approved by on-call manager: (A) Deploy temporary kernel-fallback flag that forces previously stable kernel for affected model family; (B) Adjust coalescer window to prefer smaller microbatches for short prompts; (C) Place per-tenant prefetch throttle for top-10 impacted customers. Rolling out to a small canary subset in hosted region us-west-2.

2026-03-10 13:30 UTC — Canary rollout began (5% traffic). Early metrics: tokens/sec recovered +33% on canary, TTFT improved -130ms median. No error rate increase. SEs notified customers in queue about gradual remediation. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4581

2026-03-10 15:10 UTC — Observability update: added a short-lived dashboard to track per-model kernel path distribution, microbatch size histogram, per-tenant KV-prefetch queue depth. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/latency/surge-rescue?org=infra

2026-03-11 01:05 UTC — Dedicated/private customers: ops alerted via runbook and provided per-cluster toggle for kernel-fallback and coalescer window. Private clusters in customer labs applied toggles; initial feedback positive (tokens/sec +25%). Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/rescue-runbook

2026-03-11 09:40 UTC — Rollout to 100% hosted traffic completed after staged verification. Post-rollout monitoring shows tokens/sec back to baseline across most models; two long-context variants still show residual ~10% throughput loss — investigating model-specific kernel mismatch.

2026-03-12 10:00 UTC — Postmortem outline started. Root cause draft: a recent kernel-ranking heuristic (runtime-1.19.3) mis-ranked int8 sparse-attention kernels for common mixed-length microbatches. The heuristic favored kernels with lower steady-state throughput at the observed sequence distribution, degrading multiplexed token throughput. Contributing factor: reduced telemetry on per-kernel QPS during last canary due to metric label collapse.

2026-03-12 10:15 UTC — Next steps: (1) build permanent kernel selector fix (ENG-#TBD), (2) add automated canary checks for per-kernel tokens/sec and TTFT regressions, (3) expand prefetch backpressure guardrails and expose per-tenant knobs in Console for enterprise customers, (4) schedule customer-specific retro calls and SLA credit assessments.

2026-03-12 10:30 UTC — Communications: CS drafted customer-facing incident summary and mitigation timeline; Legal and Sales reviewing. Incident postmortem owner assigned: Riley Chen. Customer-facing note: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/2026-03-09-token-regression/summary.docx
